A portable volatile memory acquisition tool for Linux

Usage: avml <COMMAND>

Commands:
  acquire  Acquire a memory snapshot to a local file (and optionally upload it)
  convert  Convert between AVML and `LiME` snapshot formats and a raw memory image
  upload   Upload an already-acquired snapshot file to remote storage
  stream   Stream a memory snapshot directly to remote storage, without writing it to a local file
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Acquire a memory snapshot to a local file (and optionally upload it)

Usage: avml acquire [OPTIONS] <FILENAME>

Arguments:
  <FILENAME>
          name of the file to write to on local system

Options:
      --compress
          compress via snappy

      --source <SOURCE>
          specify input source

          Possible values:
          - /dev/crash:  Provides a read-only view of physical memory.  Access to memory using this device must be paged aligned and read one page at a time
          - /dev/mem:    Provides a read-write view of physical memory, though AVML opens it in a read-only fashion.  Access to to memory using this device can be disabled using the kernel configuration options `CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM` or `CONFIG_IO_STRICT_DEVMEM`
          - /proc/kcore: Provides a virtual ELF coredump of kernel memory.  This can be used to access physical memory

      --max-disk-usage <MAX_DISK_USAGE>
          Specify the maximum estimated disk usage (in MiB)

      --max-disk-usage-percentage <MAX_DISK_USAGE_PERCENTAGE>
          Specify the maximum estimated disk usage to stay under

      --url <URL>
          upload via HTTP PUT upon acquisition; mutually exclusive with --sas-url

      --delete
          delete upon successful upload

      --sas-url <SAS_URL>
          upload via Azure Blob Store upon acquisition; mutually exclusive with --url

      --sas-block-size <SAS_BLOCK_SIZE>
          specify maximum block size in MiB; must be greater than 0

      --sas-block-concurrency <SAS_BLOCK_CONCURRENCY>
          specify blob upload concurrency; must be greater than 0

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Convert between AVML and `LiME` snapshot formats and a raw memory image

Usage: avml convert [OPTIONS] <SRC> <DST>

Arguments:
  <SRC>  name of the source file to read from on local system
  <DST>  name of the destination file to write to on local system

Options:
      --source-format <SOURCE_FORMAT>  specify input format [default: lime_compressed] [possible values: raw, lime, lime_compressed]
      --format <FORMAT>                specify output format [default: lime] [possible values: raw, lime, lime_compressed]
  -h, --help                           Print help

Upload an already-acquired snapshot file to remote storage

Usage: avml upload <COMMAND>

Commands:
  put   Upload a local file via HTTP PUT
  blob  Upload a local file to Azure Block Blob Storage
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Upload a local file via HTTP PUT

Usage: avml upload put <FILENAME> <URL>

Arguments:
  <FILENAME>  name of the file to upload on the local system
  <URL>       url to upload via HTTP PUT

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Upload a local file to Azure Block Blob Storage

Usage: avml upload blob [OPTIONS] <FILENAME> <URL>

Arguments:
  <FILENAME>  name of the file to upload on the local system
  <URL>       SAS URL identifying the destination Block Blob

Options:
      --sas-block-concurrency <SAS_BLOCK_CONCURRENCY>
          specify blob upload concurrency; must be greater than 0
      --sas-block-size <SAS_BLOCK_SIZE>
          specify maximum block size in MiB; must be greater than 0
  -h, --help
          Print help

Stream a memory snapshot directly to remote storage, without writing it to a local file

Usage: avml stream <COMMAND>

Commands:
  blob  Stream to Azure Block Blob Storage via `stage_block` + `commit_block_list`
  tcp   Stream to a remote TCP listener (e.g. `nc -l PORT > snapshot.lime`)
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Stream to Azure Block Blob Storage via `stage_block` + `commit_block_list`

Usage: avml stream blob [OPTIONS] <SAS_URL>

Arguments:
  <SAS_URL>
          SAS URL identifying the destination Block Blob

Options:
      --compress
          compress via snappy

      --source <SOURCE>
          specify input source. If unset, the source is probed once at start (kcore, then /dev/crash, then /dev/mem); the choice cannot be changed once any bytes have been written

          Possible values:
          - /dev/crash:  Provides a read-only view of physical memory.  Access to memory using this device must be paged aligned and read one page at a time
          - /dev/mem:    Provides a read-write view of physical memory, though AVML opens it in a read-only fashion.  Access to to memory using this device can be disabled using the kernel configuration options `CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM` or `CONFIG_IO_STRICT_DEVMEM`
          - /proc/kcore: Provides a virtual ELF coredump of kernel memory.  This can be used to access physical memory

      --sas-block-size <SAS_BLOCK_SIZE>
          minimum block size in MiB. The actual block size may be larger if needed to keep the total block count below Azure's 50,000 limit

      --sas-block-concurrency <SAS_BLOCK_CONCURRENCY>
          maximum number of in-flight `stage_block` calls

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Stream to a remote TCP listener (e.g. `nc -l PORT > snapshot.lime`).

The destination is opened with a single `connect`; on connection failure mid-stream the snapshot aborts without retry.

Usage: avml stream tcp [OPTIONS] <ADDR>

Arguments:
  <ADDR>
          destination TCP listener as host:port. Hostnames are resolved

Options:
      --compress
          compress via snappy

      --source <SOURCE>
          specify input source. If unset, the source is probed once at start (kcore, then /dev/crash, then /dev/mem); the choice cannot be changed once any bytes have been written

          Possible values:
          - /dev/crash:  Provides a read-only view of physical memory.  Access to memory using this device must be paged aligned and read one page at a time
          - /dev/mem:    Provides a read-write view of physical memory, though AVML opens it in a read-only fashion.  Access to to memory using this device can be disabled using the kernel configuration options `CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM` or `CONFIG_IO_STRICT_DEVMEM`
          - /proc/kcore: Provides a virtual ELF coredump of kernel memory.  This can be used to access physical memory

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
